title: AI-ML based Intelligent Dead Reckoning system for seamless navigation
department: Department of Space / Indian Space Research Organisation
dataset_link: IO-VNBD: Inertial and Odometry benchmark dataset for ground vehicle positioning (https://github.com/onyekpeu/IO-VNBD)
description:
Background Vehicle logistics, ride-hailing services, quick commerce and emergency responders heavily rely on smartphone-based navigation apps (like Google Maps or MapmyIndia) powered by GNSS (GPS/Galileo/NavIC etc). However, when a vehicle enters a long underground tunnel/ underpass, a multi-level parking lot, a dense forested highway, or a deep urban canyon surrounded by skyscrapers, GNSS connectivity drops entirely. GNSS signals are inherently weak and vulnerable to structural blockage (urban canyons, dense foliage, tunnels, deep valleys) and unintentional electromagnetic interferences from variety of sources such as jamming. This causes navigation apps to freeze, jump erratically, or miscalculate upcoming turns, leading to missed exits, delivery delays, and safety hazards.
In these environments, systems must rely on self-contained Inertial Navigation Systems (INS) built from Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) (accelerometers and gyroscopes) to calculate position via dead reckoning during GNSS outage and switch back to GNSS aided INS after blackout. While INS is immune to external jamming, low-cost tactical or MEMS-grade IMUs suffer from inherent sensor biases, deterministic errors, and thermo-mechanical noise. While modern high-end cars possess factory-fitted, wheel-connected Inertial Navigation Systems (INS), the vast majority of vehicles on Indian roads-including commercial trucks, older cars, and millions of two-wheelers (motorcycles/scooters)-rely solely on the driver’s smartphone mounted on the dashboard or placed in mobile holder.
Using a smartphone's internal MEMS IMU (accelerometer and gyroscope) to track vehicle position via dead reckoning during a GNSS blackout is highly challenging. The smartphone is subjected to severe chassis vibrations, engine harmonics, sudden braking, and road potholes. Without an external speedometer feed from the vehicle's OBD-II port, calculating distance and velocity exclusively from consumer-grade smartphone sensors results in exponential error accumulation, causing the estimated location to drift away within seconds. To overcome these challenges, there is a need for AI-ML enhanced dead reckoning and sensor fusion(GNSS+INS) techniques that integrate AI and machine learning models with real-time correction strategies.
Description The goal is to develop a lightweight, edge-deployable software engine and mobile application that transforms a standalone smartphone into an Intelligent Dead Reckoning (IDR) system with GNSS Fusion. When a GNSS outage occurs, the application must instantly transition to inertial tracking(INS), maintaining lane-level accuracy without requiring any physical connection to the vehicle’s internal computer and seamlessly switch back to GNSS aided INS solution.
To bypass the need for an external speedometer, the solution must employ AI/ML models trained on vehicle kinematics to accurately predict vehicle speed and acceleration profiles solely from the smartphone’s noisy accelerometer/gyro inputs. It must dynamically detect and filter out non-navigation motions such as engine idling vibrations, pothole shocks, bumps, and accidental phone misalignments on the mount.
Furthermore, the navigation engine should implement a smart Map-Matching Filter. By overlaying the inertial trajectory onto an offline map database (e.g., Open Street Map), the system should use the road layout as a constraint. For instance, it can apply Non-Holonomic Constraints (NHC), assuming a car cannot slide sideways or fly upwards, to dramatically snap the drifting IMU path back onto the actual road grid.
Also, the GNSS+INS fusion Algorithm should employ AI/ML techniques to develop an AI based fusion model to mitigate drift errors and provide accurate position.
The Final solution and AI/ML models developed should not be constricted to smart phone IMU sensors data alone (Mobile application). These algorithms/models should also work with any other external IMU sensors data (Edge deployable software engine).
Dataset Details: IO-VNBD: Inertial and Odometry benchmark dataset for ground vehicle positioning.
This dataset should be used to train & test the models and submit for screening of proposals. Teams are required to include the preliminary AI models and the results of the position plot inferenced from the subset of IO-VNBD dataset as part of their proposals submitted for evaluation. During the screening process more datasets will be provided for further evaluation of the AI models.
The On-Device Workflow Dead reckoning and GNSS fusion algorithms are hybrid. Complex training happens in the cloud/desktop apriori, while inference happens on the smartphone.
1. Model Training (Cloud/Desktop): Teams should train AI-ML models using IMU sensors datasets collected using a smartphone mounted on their vehicles or datasets available in open-source domain (for eg. ‘IO-VNBD dataset’) and bring trained models with them for SIH finale. Teams can bring the downloaded map database (e.g., Open Street Map).
2. On-Device Execution (Smartphone): During SIH Finale, the trained, lightweight model will need to be exported to the smartphone. It should receive live inputs from the phone's built-in Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)-the accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer/compass and GNSS data if available. The AI-ML based algorithms should remove IMU sensors noise & bias, predict corrections, perform map matching and determine continuous position using AI-ML based algorithms for both dead reckoning and GNSS+INS Fusion. For complete details regarding final solution, refer to the expected solution section.
Expected Solution The final deliverable must be a working mobile application and an Edge deployable software engine exhibiting the following technical capabilities:
• In-Vehicle Alignment & Calibration Engine: An algorithmic module that automatically determines the phone’s pitch, roll, and yaw relative to the vehicle's driving direction, whether the phone is strictly dashboard-mounted or placed in mobile holder.
• AI Speed & Vibration Filter: A deep-learning or statistical signal-processing model running locally on the phone that filters out high-frequency road noise/potholes and directly estimates vehicle forward velocity from IMU signals.
• Advanced Map-Matching & Kinematic Constraints: A framework (e.g., AI-ML framework or Unscented Kalman Filter + Hidden Markov Map Matching) that binds the calculated position to known road networks and geometric paths during a dropout.
• GNSS+INS Fusion Engine: An innovative AI based Sensor Fusion Algorithm that combines GNSS & IMU measurements and provides significant improvement in overall output by eliminating drift errors and providing accurate position and velocity.
• Seamless GNSS Deficit Handler: An instant seamless transition mechanism between GNSS aided INS and Dead reckoning modes within milliseconds of GNSS signal blackout and vice-versa.
• Real-time Navigation Interface: A functional mobile application with UI displaying a smooth, uninterrupted vehicle icon showing seamless navigation.
Performance Benchmark:
Dead Reckoning: The solution must restrict positional drift to less than 10% of the total distance travelled using smartphone IMUs sensors during GNSS signals blackout (for e.g., in case of smartphones IMU, a drift of less than 5 meters is desired over 50m GNSS denied environment in <1 minutes OR less than 100m of drift over a 1km GNSS denied environment at a speed of 60kmph in tunnels/underground metro OR similar simulated environments where GNSS signals are unavailable).
GNSS+INS Fusion: Position update rate of 10Hz with processing on smartphones (Mobile application) and higher update rates on Edge deployable software engine using FOG based IMU sensors data (around 200Hz).
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, machine learning applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on sensor, model, real-time. Sustainability (5/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 26/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-ML Based Intelligent Dead Reckoning System for Seamless Navigation

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a navigation system that uses AI to correct the drift and errors inherent in cheap phone-grade motion sensors, so a vehicle's position stays accurate using only inertial sensors when GPS drops out in tunnels, parking garages, or dense forests, then seamlessly hands back to GPS when signal returns.
overview.why_it_matters: GPS failures cause real navigation problems, missed exits, delivery delays, safety hazards, for logistics, ride-hailing, and emergency services. AI-corrected dead reckoning genuinely solves the gap where low-cost sensors alone drift too much to be useful.
pain_points: GNSS signals fail entirely in tunnels, parking garages, dense forest, and urban canyons, and are vulnerable to jamming.
Low-cost MEMS-grade IMUs have inherent sensor biases and error drift that accumulates over time.
Navigation apps freeze, jump erratically, or miscalculate turns during GNSS outages, causing real operational problems.
overview.background: Smartphone-based navigation apps rely heavily on GNSS, but signal loss in tunnels, garages, and dense environments causes real navigation failures, and low-cost IMUs used for dead reckoning suffer from drift that current systems don't adequately correct.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI/ML-based dead reckoning system using low-cost IMU data to maintain accurate position during GNSS outages, with seamless GNSS-INS handoff and re-acquisition.
expected_solution: AI/ML-based sensor bias and drift correction for low-cost MEMS IMUs.
Dead reckoning position/heading estimation during GNSS outage.
Seamless switching between GNSS-aided and pure INS modes.
Validated accuracy over realistic outage durations and scenarios (tunnels, parking, forest).

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. AI/ML-based correction of MEMS IMU drift for smartphone-grade dead reckoning is a genuine, active research and product area (relevant to real navigation companies), real technical sophistication.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real understanding of INS error models, sensor fusion (typically Kalman-filter-based, with AI/ML enhancement), and genuine field-testing/validation, substantial technical depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine sensor fusion/navigation engineering expertise, a specialized field, though this is one of the highest-scoring PS in the entire dataset.

innovation.note: AI/ML-enhanced dead reckoning for consumer-grade sensors is genuine, valuable, actively-relevant technical territory.

invention.note: Combining INS error modeling with ML-based bias/drift correction is substantial, real sensor-fusion engineering depth.

technical_feasibility.note: Smartphone IMU data is accessible for collection, and established sensor-fusion techniques (Kalman filtering) provide a foundation to enhance with ML.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly addresses a widespread, real-world navigation failure affecting logistics, delivery, ride-hailing, and emergency response at genuine scale.

architecture.note: Sensor fusion architecture with ML-enhanced correction and GNSS-INS mode switching, real but well-understood pattern given established navigation engineering foundations.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, the highest-scoring PS in this batch, genuinely well-motivated with clear, relatable real-world stakes and comfortable feasibility given accessible smartphone sensor data and established sensor-fusion techniques to build on.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: You can collect your own real smartphone IMU data by walking or driving through actual GNSS-degraded environments (tunnels, garages), giving genuine real test data, not synthetic.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without genuine field testing in real GNSS-degraded conditions, claimed accuracy improvements would be unvalidated, this needs real, physical data collection, not simulation alone.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Collect real smartphone IMU and GNSS data by physically walking/driving through a real GNSS-degraded environment (a tunnel, parking garage, or forested area near you) to validate your dead-reckoning accuracy against real outage scenarios, not just simulated data.

idea_0_4: Plan real data collection: identify a real GNSS-degraded environment (tunnel, parking garage) near you for test data collection.
Research established INS/dead-reckoning error models and sensor-fusion techniques (Kalman filtering) as your foundation.
Split: one person on data collection/sensor-fusion baseline, one on the ML-based correction layer.
prototype_4_22: Collect real smartphone IMU and GNSS data walking/driving through your test environment, capturing the transition into and out of GNSS outage.
Build your baseline dead-reckoning system (standard Kalman-filter-based INS) as a comparison point.
Build your ML-based bias/drift correction layer enhancing the baseline.
integration_22_30: Test your ML-enhanced system against your baseline on your real collected outage data, measuring position error over the outage duration.
Test the GNSS-INS handoff/re-acquisition smoothness at both entry and exit of the outage.
Refine based on real test results.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization comparing your ML-enhanced dead reckoning against the baseline and against a GPS ground-truth reference where available.
Rehearse presenting your real collected data and measured accuracy improvement.
Prepare to discuss your approach's real-world applicability across the named use cases (logistics, ride-hailing, emergency response).
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Present real position-error data from your own physically-collected GNSS-outage test, your ML-enhanced approach compared directly against a standard Kalman-filter baseline over the same real outage, that genuine field validation with real measured improvement is exactly the kind of concrete evidence this PS's high potential deserves.

strengths: Real smartphone sensor data is directly collectable for genuine field validation.
Established sensor-fusion techniques provide a strong, well-understood foundation to enhance with ML.
weaknesses: Genuine field data collection takes real time and planning, don't leave it until late in the build.
MEMS IMU drift correction is a real, hard engineering problem, meaningful improvement over a good baseline is a genuine achievement, not a given.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Navigation-engineering-weighted, with real ML skill for the correction layer.
team_fit.approach: Plan and execute real data collection early, this is your most valuable asset and takes real physical time to gather properly.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing genuinely effective ML-based bias/drift correction grounded in real IMU error characteristics, and validating against real collected field data, that requires real sensor-fusion and navigation engineering expertise.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An ML correction layer validated only on simulated/synthetic drift patterns without real field testing wouldn't demonstrate genuine improvement on the actual, messy sensor noise real smartphones produce.

data_resource_availability.status: Real smartphone IMU and GNSS data is directly collectable through your own physical data collection in real GNSS-degraded environments.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If physical data collection in a genuinely GNSS-degraded environment isn't feasible, use publicly available INS/GNSS benchmark datasets if any exist, clearly noting the substitution.

judge_qna.question: Is your test data real, collected in an actual GNSS-degraded environment, or simulated?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your real data collection methodology directly, walking/driving through an actual tunnel or garage with your phone logging both IMU and GNSS data, real field data is far more credible than pure simulation.
judge_qna.follow_up: How long was your real test outage duration, and how did position error grow over that time?

judge_qna.question: How much better is your ML-enhanced approach than a standard Kalman-filter baseline, measured on the same real data?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your direct, quantified comparison, ML-enhanced versus baseline, on the same real outage data, real numbers showing the actual improvement.
judge_qna.follow_up: What specific error characteristic (bias drift, scale factor error) does your ML correction address that the baseline Kalman filter doesn't?
